# ShipQuick feedback: the whole story

Fill every section below. None may be empty — `feedback.sh` refuses and names the one you skipped.
The header (project, ShipQuick commit, date) is filled by the script; do not write it yourself.
Save this as a file and run: `knowledge/shipquick_latest/scripts/feedback.sh --title "<one line>" --body-file <this file>`

## Situation
Project, tool and version, what you were doing, the ids (PR, issue, run), the exact error text.

## Expected vs seen
What you expected to happen; what actually happened; who or what noticed it.

## Steps to reproduce
3 to 5 numbered steps, and the one command that shows it.

## Impact
How often it happens, time lost, what was blocked.

## Root cause
A five-whys chain: at least three "Why" lines, ending at the real cause.
Why 1: ...
Why 2: ...
Why 3: ...

## Why ShipQuick did not catch it
The rule, check or script that was missing or wrong.

## How big teams avoid it
The industry practice, with a source, its tier (A, B, C, K, P) and a confidence from 0 to 1.

## Generic fix for ShipQuick
The change — written for any project, no project facts. State "Applies when" and "Does not apply to".

## Stop the repeat
The test or CI check that would fail if this happens again, and the workaround the project uses today.
